THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Weston wrapped up a nearly three-decade tax increment financing district that added $354 million in assessed value, while Kronenwetter's village board approved a rezoning and moved forward on several community projects.

  • Weston's Community Development Authority voted unanimously to pay off its 2017A lease revenue bonds early, retiring debt that had been scheduled to run through 2031.
  • Weston's CDA closed TIF District No. 1 after a 28-year run that generated $95.7 million in increment; staff will bring the question of disbanding the CDA to the Village Board.
  • Kronenwetter's Village Board approved rezoning Marathon County Highway Department property to M2 General Industrial, clearing the way for the county to develop its facility there.
  • Kronenwetter's Village Board approved a Bushka Park 5K/3K run/walk fundraiser for September 12 and authorized matching a $5,000 parks grant.
  • Kronenwetter's CLIPP Committee is set to vote on a temporary moratorium on data center development applications and consider a new oak wilt ordinance.
  • The Wausau School Board is set to act on the 2026-27 teacher salary schedule and employee handbook updates at its special meeting Monday.

Coming up: Monday is a busy night — Wausau school board members meet at 5 p.m. for both a special session on teacher pay and a workshop on survey results and potential referendum considerations, while Kronenwetter's CLIPP Committee takes up the data center moratorium at 6 p.m. Later in the week, Weston's Village Board of Trustees meets Thursday, August 6.
